subject: FintechCo — Multi-region performance & competitive follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@fintechco.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery — multi-region perf requirements

Hi Emily / Carlos,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Goals: reduce end-user inference latency in APAC/EU, maintain data residency for EU customers, and evaluate unit economics vs current hyperscaler endpoints.
- Current stack: FintechCo is calling a managed inference API in us-east for risk scoring. You see ~120ms p95 for single-shard calls from US, ~240ms p95 from EU, and ~300ms p95 from APAC (observed from your client-side instrumentation).
- Constraints: PCI-adjacent data controls in EU, procurement prefers SaaS but will consider dedicated or VPC if residency/SLA controls are needed.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Run a short multi-region performance eval: p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm start, and throughput tail at 10TPS and 100TPS across regions.
2) Produce a short comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoint (we'll instrument from the same geographic points you use).
3) Deliver a SLO proposal (latency targets and fallbacks) + a cost delta estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

If that sounds right I can schedule the tests for next week. I attached a brief test plan (redwood_test_plan.md) — it lists the endpoints we'll hit, regions, and expected metrics.

What I need from you to get started:
- Confirmation you can enable the test IP ranges below (we'll keep the traffic low and labeled).
- A short list of representative endpoints (paths) and a sample request body for scoring so we can replicate payloads.

Proposed times to start tests: Tue 2026-06-22 or Wed 2026-06-23 (US morning). Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Intro + discovery — multi-region perf requirements

Emily — perfect, thanks. We'll plan to start Tue 2026-06-22 at 09:00 PT. A few follow-ups inline and a short competitive summary attached.

Quick answers to procurement question (summary):
- Latency: Redwood's hosted API runs in-region endpoints (us-east1, europe-west1, asia-east1) and can route traffic to the closest region with <10ms added network hop when the model is co-located. Hyperscaler-managed endpoints often have similar in-region latencies but have more variability depending on gpu provisioning and cold starts — our continuous batching and KV cache reduces p95 tail for recurrent sessions.
- Cold start behavior: Redwood's runtime maintains warm model instances for low-latency tiers; Dedicated and Private options allow reserved capacity to eliminate cold starts. Hyperscalers may require larger node sizes or provisioned concurrency for similar behavior which can increase cost.
- Data residency & controls: We offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments and a Dedicated option with region-locking and customer-managed KMS for EU residency.
- Cost: We'll provide a quick TCO scoping — hosted per-token + regional data transfer vs Dedicated commit. See attached redwood_vs_hyperscaler-summary.pdf for the short bullets and a sample TCO worksheet.

Test plan notes:
- We'll instrument from the same vantage points you shared.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization on our side, queue times, and error rates.
- Deliverables: perf report, raw traces, suggested config (batching/quantization) to hit your p95 SLO, and a draft SLO doc.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler-summary.pdf (short competitive bullets + sample TCO).

I'll kick off coordination with infra to reserve the run and will send a meeting invite for a quick 15-min alignment on Mon 2026-06-21 to confirm IPs and payload.

Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: FintechCo multi-region perf — internal notes

Internal — quick note before the test:

- Suggest we run two model variants: quantized fp16 and int8 (if available) to show cost/latency tradeoffs. The int8 path should materially reduce GPU memory and allow more concurrent in-region workers which can improve tail latency for high-concurrency windows.
- Sean: can infra stand up a dedicated small pool in europe-west1 for the run and enable detailed metrics export? We want GPU telemetry and per-request latency traces.
- Jordan: keep the run small (10-50 TPS) for the first pass; we'll add a 100TPS burst later.

Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@fintechco.com>

Jordan / Marissa — good alignment call this morning. We're green to begin the tests at 09:00 PT today. A few final asks:

- Please share the SLO proposal before the end of day so I can forward to procurement.
- We need a short one-page doc that highlights the differences vs AWS/GCP for procurement (latency, cold starts, residency controls). Your attached summary was useful but procurement wants a one-pager.
- Attaching our procurement initiation form — we'll kick off the internal review once we have the SLO and one-pager (slo_proposal_v2.pdf attached).

Thanks — Emily
